title: Cycle time of a batch reactor
intro:
A batch reactor's cycle time X is equally likely to be anywhere between **40** and **52 minutes**: uniform with a = 40 and b = 52.

Find the probability that a cycle takes **44 minutes or less**, the probability that it takes **between 44 and 50 minutes**, and the mean and standard deviation of the cycle time. Give the probabilities to three decimals or more and the mean and standard deviation to two decimals.

AtMost.says: That is the height of the density, 1/(b − a). A probability is an area: multiply the height by the width of the interval, 44 − 40.
That is P(X > 44), the area to the right of 44. "44 minutes or less" is the area to the left: (44 − a)/(b − a).

StandardDeviation.says: That is the variance, (b − a)²/12. The standard deviation is its square root.
You took the square root of (b − a)/12. The variance squares the width first: (b − a)²/12.

hints: The density is a rectangle of height 1/(b − a) = 1/12 between 40 and 52.
A probability is the width of the interval times the height: P(44 ≤ X ≤ 50) = (50 − 44)/12.
